about: La Aurora's 107th anniversary blend from 2010, built on a sun grown Ecuadorian wrapper over Dominican binder and a mixed filler. It starts mild and builds to medium-full, and became one of the company's core lines.
notes: The maker now sells it as 107 Ecuador; the band just reads 107. Halfwheel lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian Sumatra (Habano sun grown in 2010) and adds Brazilian filler. The maker's chart prints the Lancero at 6 1/8 x 40; halfwheel lists 6 7/8 x 40. Some U.S. retailers list the Robusto at 4 1/2 x 50 and the strength as medium.
verifyNotes: Blend, sizes and strength (text says medium to full, gauge 80/100) checked on the maker page and size chart. Lancero kept at 6 7/8 per halfwheel but the maker chart prints 6 1/8, now noted. Note corrected: halfwheel's Habano listing is from 2010, not 2011, and only some retailers (Famous) list the Robusto at 4 1/2. Swapped the Neptune link for the halfwheel Lancero review that backs the Lancero size.

about: The first Nicaraguan puro from La Aurora, blended by Manuel Inoa and rolled in the Dominican Republic. It is the Nicaragua entry in the 107 Tobaccos of the World series.
notes: All Nicaraguan tobacco but rolled in the Dominican Republic. The maker's chart shows the Toro at 5 1/2 x 54 and Churchill at 7 x 47; halfwheel lists 5 3/4 x 54 and 7 x 50. Only Robusto, Toro and Gran Toro launched in the U.S. Strength is disputed: the maker's gauge reads 85/100 and Neptune says full; Famous Smoke and halfwheel say medium.
verifyNotes: Wrapper, binder and filler confirmed in Cigar Aficionado; country and factory in halfwheel; sizes on the maker chart. Strength left as Full (maker gauge 85/100, Neptune) but the note now says Famous Smoke lists medium and that the Churchill size differs between maker and halfwheel.

about: The third blend in La Aurora's value-priced Time Capsule (Original Blends) series, launched in 2017. The name honors 1903, the year the company was founded and says it first worked with Cameroon wrapper.
notes: The maker says the wrapper is now Cameroon seed grown in Ecuador; halfwheel, Cigar Aficionado and retailers list it simply as Cameroon. The U.S. launch had four sizes (Robusto, Toro, Churchill, Gran Toro); the maker's chart adds Belicoso, Cetros, Corona and tubed versions.

about: One of the two original Time Capsule (Original Blends) cigars from 2016, wrapped in Dominican-grown corojo. The year marks when La Aurora says it began blending with corojo wrapper.
notes: The maker's text describes the strength as medium to strong, but its own gauge reads 60/100 and Famous Smoke and Neptune list it as medium. At the 2016 launch the Churchill was 7 x 50 and the Toro 5 1/2 x 54; the maker now lists 7 x 47 and 5 3/4 x 54.
verifyNotes: All fields confirmed on the maker page, halfwheel and Cigar Aficionado. Strength kept as Medium-Full on the maker's wording, but added to the note that the maker's gauge is 60/100 and both retailers say medium.

about: The Connecticut-wrapped member of La Aurora's Time Capsule (Original Blends) series, launched in 2016 alongside the 1962 Corojo. The year marks when La Aurora says it began blending with Connecticut wrapper.
notes: The maker lists an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper, Ecuadorian binder and Peruvian leaf in the filler. Halfwheel, Cigar Aficionado and retailers list a Dominican binder with Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, and Neptune calls the wrapper U.S. Connecticut Shade. Retailers split between mild and medium.

about: The fourth Time Capsule (Original Blends) cigar, released in 2019 with a Brazilian maduro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. It is the fullest of the series and priced as an everyday smoke.
notes: Early descriptions, still used by some retailers, list Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler; the distributor corrected it to all Nicaraguan. The maker's chart shows the Toro at 5 1/2 x 54 and adds a 41 ring Cetros; halfwheel lists the Toro at 5 3/4 x 54.

about: The Connecticut-wrapped version of Preferidos, La Aurora's top line, best known for its tubed double figurado. It is the mildest of the Preferidos blends.
notes: The maker now brands Preferidos as the 1903 Edition and calls this blend Connecticut on the straight sizes. The maker's chart lists the Toro at 5 3/4 x 54; halfwheel and Famous Smoke list 5 1/2 x 54.

about: The Brazilian maduro version of Preferidos, La Aurora's top line, best known for its tubed double figurado. Straight sizes were added in 2017.
notes: The maker now brands Preferidos as the 1903 Edition and calls this blend Maduro on the straight sizes. The maker's chart lists the Toro at 5 3/4 x 54; halfwheel and Famous Smoke list 5 1/2 x 54.
verifyNotes: Blend and strength confirmed on both maker pages. Replaced the Famous Smoke link with the maker's parejo page, which is where the straight sizes come from.

filler: Dominican Republic (Cibao Valley), Brazil, Nicaragua, Peru
about: The Ecuadorian Sumatra version of Preferidos, La Aurora's top line, best known for its tubed double figurado. The maker describes it as earthy, spicy and medium bodied.
notes: The maker now brands Preferidos as the 1903 Edition and calls this blend Ecuador on the straight sizes. The maker's chart lists the Toro at 5 3/4 x 54; Famous Smoke lists 5 1/2 x 54.
verifyNotes: Blend and strength confirmed on both maker pages. Renamed the 6 x 58 size: Famous Smoke sells it as Ecuador #1, a perfecto; no source calls it Doble Figurado No. 1. It is not on the maker's chart.

filler: Dominican Republic (Cibao Valley and andullo), Pennsylvania (USA), Nicaragua
about: A La Aurora line built around andullo, a traditional Dominican tobacco that is cured pressed inside palm-pod rolls instead of in piles. A full leaf of andullo goes into the filler of each cigar; the name means Dominican DNA.
notes: Not a Dominican puro: the binder is Cameroon and the filler includes Pennsylvania and Nicaraguan leaf. The wrapper's seed type is not published. Famous Smoke lists it as full in its specs and medium-full in its description; halfwheel's reviewer found it medium.

about: The regular-production cigar marking 115 years since La Aurora's founding in 1903. It pairs an Ecuadorian wrapper with a Brazilian binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Brazilian filler.
notes: Sold in the U.S. as the 115th Anniversary. This is the regular line; a separate limited edition (announced 2018, in the U.S. in 2019) used a Dominican corojo wrapper and reached the U.S. only as a Belicoso and Gran Toro. The maker and halfwheel say only that the wrapper is Ecuadorian; Famous Smoke calls it Habano.
verifyNotes: Blend and sizes confirmed on the maker page and halfwheel; strength Full is from Famous Smoke (maker gauge 80/100). Habano rests on Famous Smoke alone. Note corrected: the limited edition was also announced in other sizes, only two reached the U.S.

notes: The cigar is real, but it is Karl Malone's own brand, made for him at the La Aurora factory and released in 2019, not a La Aurora line. Halfwheel lists Ecuadorian wrapper and binder with Dominican, Nicaraguan and Peruvian filler. La Aurora's own Barrel Aged is a different cigar.
verifyNotes: Second attempt made: it is not on La Aurora's product list, Famous Smoke's La Aurora Barrel Aged is a different Dominican corojo cigar, and halfwheel files it as Malone's own brand. Left found false; added the halfwheel blend to the note.

about: The second line from Tony Bellatto's La Barba, released in 2014 and blended with help from Robert Caldwell and Henderson Ventura. It was dropped in 2022 after a fire destroyed the factory that made it.
notes: Discontinued in October 2022 after the Tabacalera William Ventura fire, so only leftover stock remains. A 6 x 54 Toro was part of the launch and was dropped in 2016.

about: La Barba's first maduro blend, released in 2018 by Tony Bellatto with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper over an Indonesian binder. It grew into a small family with later Mexi-Sol and Shade versions.
notes: Announced as Primitivo and renamed before shipping over a trademark conflict. The original orange-band blend is also called Ricochet Crü Oscuro. Neptune calls it medium; halfwheel's review found medium-full strength building to full. After the 2022 fire at Tabacalera William Ventura, production moved to the Ventura family's El Maestro factory.
verifyNotes: All fields confirmed in halfwheel and Neptune. Added that production moved to El Maestro after the 2022 factory fire, per halfwheel.
